items.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023
items.q: John Coltrane gave us “My Favorite Things” but he also gave us “A Love Supreme.” ... somehow this John Coltrane entered the recording session

ctx.x: Oh originality. Oh I’m glad you read that. There was a film that I happened to stumble into, Liza Manelli — it might have been “Arthur” but I’m not sure if it was “Arthur.” But the very last scene she’s in a fur coat, she’s the star, and there’s like it’s the end of the film and everyone is like “Liza, Liza, Liza.” And she gets into the limo and a little girl stops her before she gets into the car. And the little girl says, “Liza” and she turns around and of course there’s this cute little girl. And the cute…

As do I. And I have great respect — you know I’ve often felt that every major city in the United States has any number of singers who are blessed with a great voice. But for me the fact that you write your own music, you do your charts, you put all this effort into it, good for you. It’s the best. I’m not sure how to express my admiration for it, but I’m trying. items.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023
items.q: And I knew that my concept of this record had to do with modern ancestors, okay, not the Sojourner Truths but the John Coltranes and the Miles Davises and the Nina Simones, okay, and the Carmen McRaes and so forth and so on.

ctx.x: Well you know I’ve done a little studio work over the years and when I was watching “Eye of the Storm” and some of your songs have rubato sections, extended sections and then you hit something new, something changes. And I was envisioning the musicians trying to play if you weren’t there. And that would be very difficult it seems.

Well so I have always recorded — I record everything I do. Okay? I record every idea I have. And I have for decades. And I just kind of change with the formatting. So if it was a four-track cassette back in the day or whatever it was, a four-track reel to reel, and then it became an A-dat, then it became this, that and the other. So I’ve always recorded. And in the last I would say the last eight or nine projects of mine I pre-record every idea I have. So I started out using what they call plug-ins or those…

software and fake, you know like they’re loops of instruments but they repeat and repeat and repeat. And they kind of support your idea but they don’t really play your song. So I got away from that. I got away from borrowing, you know bossa nova 101 and all that stuff, and began to play the drums myself and play the bass and play the piano, play the guitar. So I would record that. I would record my drums. Record the bass. Sometimes it would be keyboard bass, sometimes I would actually pick up one of the basses.…
